name: What happens if demolition reveals mold, rot, or water damage behind the bathroom wall?

mainEntity.name: What happens if demolition reveals mold, rot, or water damage behind the bathroom wall?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you find water damage after demolition, pause decisions that would cover the area and document what is visible. The source may involve a supply line, drain, shower waterproofing, toilet connection, window, roof condition, or long-term condensation, and the correct repair depends on the cause. The affected framing, subfloor, insulation, and adjacent finishes may also need evaluation. Ask for a revised scope that distinguishes investigation, drying or removal, structural repair, and replacement work. Elite Remodeling & Design can reassess the design-build plan when concealed conditions change the original scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Stop covering the area and identify the moisture source before rebuilding. Damage may involve plumbing, waterproofing, a window, ventilation, or another adjacent condition, with possible effects on framing and subflooring. Request a documented change in scope separating investigation, removal, repair, drying, and replacement.
